newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel ends sharply lower against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel ends sharply lower against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel fell sharply against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies on Tuesday for the second consecutive day amid strong demand from the business sector, dealers said.
"Activity was relatively high today and the trend was very clear. The business sector is closing positions and repaying dollar-linked loans," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.
"The market believes that inflation will fall in the near future and that interest rates will decline. This makes the dollar-linked loans less attractive and more risky," he added.
Dealers said that when the U.S. currency reached 3.30 shekels investors started selling dolllars.
The dollar began rising on Monday against the shekel from a rate of 3.253 on Friday. There is no foreign currency trading in Israel on Sunday.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2920 shekels against 3.2730 on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.6702 shekels against 3.6641 on Monday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8867 shekels per 100 yen versus 2.8804 on Monday and against the mark at 2.1062 shekels versus 2.1219 on Monday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2980 shekels.
